solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Translucent boil mostly having an uneven surface

indicators.note: 'mostly' means most of it but not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: seethe = boil, minus its last E
the rough, as on a golf course, is uneven ground

explanation.surface: A description of a nasty skin blister, pale and bumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a medical note about a boil; 'boil' is really the verb, as in water seething.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: fabric that lets light through, so you can almost see through it, is translucent.

clue.text: Bargain hunter finding fish higher in price!

explanation.surface: A shopper at the fishmonger's discovers the fish has gone up in price.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from Shakespeare's Autolycus, 'a snapper-up of unconsidered trifles'; the exclamation mark flags the shopper's dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary idiom: someone who grabs goods the moment they appear cheap is exactly what a bargain hunter is.

clue.text: Old academic flipped over introduction of standardised tests

indicators.note: something flipped over lies the other way up, so in a down entry its letters run in reverse

parts.note: MA, a Master of Arts, turned round

indicators.note: the introduction is the opening of a thing, so take the word's first letter

explanation.surface: An elderly professor loses his temper at the arrival of standardised testing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipped' sounds like losing one's temper; it only turns MA round. EX is the usual crossword prefix for 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: school and university tests, especially formal written ones, are called exams.

clue.text: Pity each revolutionary's grief

indicators.note: a revolution overturns the existing order, so the letters of EACH do not stay in theirs

parts.note: heart = compassion, as in 'have a heart'

explanation.surface: A lament for the sorrow each revolutionary carries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' reads as a noun, a rebel; it is an adjective telling you to rearrange EACH. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the emotional pain of loss or disappointment, felt as if in the chest, is grief.

clue.text: Experiencing a spell of good luck when student managed to block toilet up

definitions.text: Experiencing a spell of good luck

indicators.note: a blockage sits inside a pipe
in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run in reverse

explanation.surface: A lucky streak for a student who manages to block the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: Assemble L + LO(RAN)O = LLORANO, then read it upwards. 'Block toilet up' pretends to be a plumbing mishap, and a toilet roll lurks in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a gambler on a roll keeps winning, so it means enjoying a run of good luck.

clue.text: German porkies describing soldiers' triumphs

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round it

parts.note: porkies = pork pies, rhyming slang for lies

explanation.surface: German propaganda exaggerating the army's victories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porkies' is British slang for lies, from the rhyming slang pork pies. 'Describing' looks like narrating the soldiers' deeds; it means drawing round them.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: past triumphs are the glories of a career or an army.

clue.text: Greek god's accuser apparently hiding on the way back

indicators.note: something hiding is tucked inside other words, here inside 'accuser apparently'
going back means travelling the other way, so read the letters from right to left

parts.note: accuSER Apparently, read right to left

explanation.surface: A god's accuser seems to be lying low as he returns home.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', so 'Greek god' is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A proper name: the Greek god of war, whom the Romans called Mars.

clue.text: Relating to a religious movement of friars at a bash

indicators.note: to bash something is to knock it out of shape, so the letters before it are knocked about

explanation.surface: Friars letting their hair down at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bash' reads as a party, the friars' night out; it is the instruction to knock the letters about.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the Jamaican religious movement is also used as its adjective, as in 'Rastafari beliefs'.

clue.text: Maiden cutting a little flower

indicators.note: a thing cutting into another sits within it

parts.note: M = maiden, a cricket over with no runs

explanation.surface: A young woman snipping a small bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword's river, something that flows. M for maiden comes from cricket scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: a flower is anything that flows, and the Somme flows through northern France.

clue.text: A literary sub-genre, on the other hand, not concerned with pursuing fun

indicators.note: being 'in' something means being concerned with it, so remove the letters IN
a pursuer comes behind what it chases, so this piece follows the other

parts.words: on the other hand, not concerned with
parts.note: again = on the other hand, minus IN

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a kind of fiction as not about having fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'A' does double duty, in the definition and the wordplay. An Aga is a British cast-iron cooking range, the emblem of the comfortable country kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A named genre: Aga sagas are novels about middle-class English country life, named after the kitchen range.

clue.text: Marsupial mouse endlessly swimming across river heading south

indicators.note: without an end, so the word loses its last letter
the rearranged letters stretch across the next pieces, enclosing them
things swimming move about freely, so the letters are rearranged
a heading is a compass direction, here south

explanation.surface: A small marsupial swims across a river heading south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marsupial mouse' reads as one creature, but the definition is 'Marsupial' alone; the mouse is raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the opossum of the Americas carries its young in a pouch, so it is a marsupial.

clue.text: Evident in Robin's charm

indicators.note: what is evident in something can be seen within it, so look inside the next word

explanation.surface: Robin's charm is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charm' suggests charisma; it is the object, a magic token.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: in the Caribbean, obi (or obeah) is folk sorcery, and also a charm or fetish used in it.

clue.text: Put forward as fact in online comment embracing individualism at the outset

indicators.note: an embrace wraps arms around someone, so the comment holds the letter inside
the outset is the very start, so take the first letter

explanation.surface: Someone online asserting the virtues of individualism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Online comment' is a noun here, a forum post, though the surface lets it read as the setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in philosophy: to assume something as a basis for argument is to put it forward as fact.

clue.text: Start to hold forth about Gail oddly back at home

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the speech goes around the rest

parts.note: orate = hold forth, make a speech

indicators.note: take the odd-numbered letters, first and third
going back means reversing, so those letters run the other way

parts.note: GaIl's odd letters G, I, reversed

explanation.surface: Gail, strangely, has started lecturing everyone back at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like a comment on Gail's behaviour; it picks her odd letters. 'Back at home' reads as a phrase but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to originate is to begin or come into being, which is to start.

clue.text: Unnamed cardinal surprisingly thorough

indicators.note: unnamed means without a name, and N is the abbreviation for name, so remove N
something turning out surprisingly is not in the expected order, so rearrange

explanation.surface: An anonymous cardinal proves unexpectedly thorough.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'unnamed cardinal' sounds like an anonymous Vatican source; it is CARDINAL with N removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: radical comes from Latin radix, root, so a radical change goes to the root and is thorough.

clue.text: Become extremely agitated and tense after literary Lorna's letter

indicators.note: a thing placed after another comes later

parts.note: Lorna Doone, heroine of Blackmore's novel

explanation.surface: Lorna Doone's letter makes someone agitated and tense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like correspondence; it is the Greek letter. 'Tense' looks like a mood; it is the grammatical abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional idiom: British slang for flying into a rage, the nut being one's head.

clue.text: Shame about American bear

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the shame goes around the American

explanation.surface: Embarrassment about an American bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' pretends to be the animal, fitting 'American'; it is the verb, to carry or endure.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to sustain weight or losses is to bear them.

clue.text: That baked dish included in South Carolina exhibition primarily as a fine example of its type

indicators.note: things included in a group sit within it, so these letters go inside the state
primarily means first of all, so take the first letter

parts.note: that = how, as in 'she told me that/how he left'
a pie is a baked dish

explanation.surface: A pie on show at a South Carolina fair, held up as the best of its kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That' can stand in for 'how' in reported speech; it is the hardest piece to see.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a showpiece is the item put on display because it is outstanding, a fine example of its type.

clue.text: Information turned over by the French court newspaper boss disregarded

indicators.note: something turned over is upside down, so in a down entry its letters read in reverse

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor ignores information handed over by a French court.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something neglected has been ignored or not attended to, that is, disregarded.

clue.text: Went without my turn to advance

indicators.note: to turn is to face the other way, so the letters run backwards
in its old sense of outside, so the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: cor! = my!, both exclamations of surprise, reversed

explanation.surface: Someone missed their turn before moving on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking; here it means outside. 'Went' is a coy euphemism, and 'cor' is a British exclamation like 'my!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to go forward or carry on is to advance.

clue.text: Think at length of Spanish gentleman keeping in good health

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the gentleman holds the health word inside him

parts.note: Don, Spanish title for a gentleman

explanation.surface: Musing about a Spanish gentleman staying healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition needs its preposition from the answer: 'think at length (of)' pairs with the phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb: to linger over a subject in thought or speech is to think at length about it.

clue.text: Wise monarch accepting immediately

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the monarch takes the other word inside

explanation.surface: A wise king agrees at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accepting immediately' reads as a prompt yes; it is a container with its contents.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a knowing look shows shrewd understanding, which is being wise.

clue.text: Of fundamental importance to mention diagram of identification at the front

indicators.note: something at the front comes first, so this piece leads even though it comes second in the clue

parts.note: a map's key identifies its symbols

explanation.surface: A caption that points to the legend of a map.
explanation.walkthrough: Used as an adjective, as in 'keynote speech'; in music the keynote is the note a key is built on, hence fundamental.
explanation.definitionFit: An attributive use: a keynote address sets out the central theme, so it is of fundamental importance.

clue.text: Betrayal of Republican entrapped by schoolmaster at end of story

indicators.note: something entrapped is caught inside
take the letter at the end of the word

explanation.surface: A Republican tricked by a teacher in a tale of betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of story' reads as a flat full stop to an argument; it gives only the Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: treachery is the betrayal of trust.

clue.text: Understood by Italian leader engaged in diplomacy

indicators.note: the leader goes first, so take the first letter
someone engaged in an activity is inside it, so the letter goes within diplomacy

explanation.surface: An Italian politician's grasp of diplomacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian leader' suggests a prime minister; it is only the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a tacit agreement is understood without being spoken aloud.

clue.text: Copper meeting resistance from scoundrel

indicators.note: two things meeting come together side by side, so the pieces join end to end

parts.note: Cu, the chemical symbol for copper
R, the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A policeman encounters resistance from a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is British slang for a police officer, which fits the scene; here it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a cur is a mongrel dog, and by extension a contemptible man, a scoundrel.

clue.text: Put in position by expert on Poland

indicators.note: in an across entry, one thing on another sits after it, so the expert follows the country

explanation.surface: Someone installed in a post by a Polish specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expert on Poland' reads as a specialist in Polish affairs; 'on' is only ordering the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to set something in a spot is to put it in position.

clue.text: Modify American person's home over time

indicators.note: something turned over faces the other way, so the home word runs backwards

parts.note: one's pad is one's home, reversed

explanation.surface: Remodelling an American's house over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pad' is slang for a flat or home. 'Over time' reads as a phrase meaning gradually, but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to change something to suit new conditions is to modify it.

clue.text: Lacking enthusiasm to take in books on royal authority

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so the cool word surrounds the rest

parts.note: NT = New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A half-hearted reader of books about royal power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Books on royal authority' reads as a reading list; the definition is only 'authority'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: having control over people means having authority over them.

clue.text: Shown openly eating Bill's ham

indicators.note: whatever is eaten ends up inside the eater, so the open word takes the bill inside it

explanation.surface: Bill is seen publicly tucking into his ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name and 'ham' like his lunch; the 's is 'is', and 'ham' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre verb: to ham is to perform with exaggerated gestures, as a bad actor does.

clue.text: Carry young child easily at first

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: 'at first' means at the very beginning, so take the word's opening letter

explanation.surface: Carrying a toddler with no trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads straight as picking up a toddler, and TOT is right there inside the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, mostly American: to tote a bag or a gun is to carry it around.

clue.text: Entire set split up before daughter becomes personally involved

indicators.note: a set that is split up is broken into pieces and scattered, so rearrange its letters
something before another comes ahead of it, so the daughter goes last

explanation.surface: A family breaks up and the daughter gets personally caught up in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split up' suggests a separation; it is the instruction to rearrange. 'Becomes' links, reading as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialised sense: an interested party has a personal stake in the outcome, not just curiosity.
